title: Questionable expenses lead to removal of delegate’s campaign treasurer
summary: House Speaker Pro Tem Luke Clippinger (D-Baltimore City) has abruptly replaced his campaign treasurer amid concerns that she misappropriated money from his campaign account.
content:
by Bryan P. Sears, Maryland Matters January 7, 2026

by Bryan P. Sears, Maryland Matters January 7, 2026

A prominent member of the House of Delegates has abruptly replaced his campaign treasurer amid concerns that she misappropriated money from his campaign account.

Del. Luke Clippinger (D-Baltimore City) told Maryland Matters he replaced Melissa Evans after being alerted to questions about $44,000 in checks written on his account and allegedly cashed by Evans.

“I am shocked and disappointed at this betrayal of trust by the treasurer of my campaign committee,” said Clippinger, the former chair of the House Judiciary Committee who was recently named speaker pro tem, the No. 2 position in the House. “I will immediately retain an accounting professional to review the treasurer’s management of my campaign account.”

Clippinger added that he has forwarded the matter to the Office of the State Prosecutor.

In a brief phone call, Clippinger referenced the open investigation and referred a reporter back to his statement.

Evans, who according to her online profile is currently employed with the Baltimore County Public Library system, did not immediately respond to a request by phone for comment.

Maryland Matters contacted Maryland State Board of Elections officials seeking clarification about Evans and her relationship with the campaign. The questions arose over 15 checks totaling $44,000 that were drawn on the account of Friends of Luke Clippinger. The checks were written over a four year period between 2020 and 2024.

All of the checks provided to Maryland Matters were made out to Evans, who appears to have endorsed the checks and deposited them into bank accounts she controlled. The checks range in amounts from $500 to two for $10,000. One of the checks was a bank check drawn on the Clippinger campaign account payable to Melissa Evans.

Evans had been Clippinger’s campaign treasurer since 2013.

Typically, campaigns do not pay their treasurers. Maryland campaign law allows for payments but requires a written agreement to be approved by the board of elections as treasurers are legally the only officer allowed to disburse funds.

A board of elections official Tuesday confirmed that no such agreement existed in the agency’s records.

Clippinger, in a statement, told Maryland Matters that board officials contacted him following that inquiry. It was then that he discovered “there were at least four checks written in the past month by my treasurer that were not authorized and not legitimate campaign expenditures.”

Those checks appear to be in addition to the $44,000 in checks obtained by Maryland Matters.

On Monday, Evans was listed as treasurer for Clippinger’s campaign.

A day later, her name had been removed. Sophia Silbergeld, who has worked as a fundraiser for Clippinger, is now listed as treasurer.
